steps.title: What Is Chaos Engineering?
steps.text: Chaos engineering proactively injects failures in controlled environments to build confidence in system resilience. Instead of waiting for production outages, you test failure modes before they happen.

steps.title: The ChaosEngine
steps.text: ChaosEngine is the central orchestrator for fault injection. It manages fault activation/deactivation, scope targeting (per broker, topic, or peer), probability-based triggering, and a timeline of all events.

steps.title: 9 Fault Types
steps.text: Surgewave supports 9 injectable faults across storage and transport layers: NetworkPartition, NodeCrash, DiskIoError, SlowNetwork, MessageCorruption, LeaderElectionDisruption, StorageFullError, ConnectionReset, and PartialWrite.

steps.title: Scenario Helpers
steps.text: High-level scenario classes compose multiple faults into realistic failure patterns. NetworkPartitionScenario isolates brokers, BrokerCrashScenario simulates crashes, and LatencyInjectionScenario adds configurable delays.

steps.title: ChaosCluster for Integration Tests
steps.text: ChaosCluster provides a multi-broker test environment with per-broker fault injection. Use convenience methods like PartitionBroker, CrashBroker, and InjectLatency to write resilience integration tests.
